summary: Ontonagon Light, a brick keeper's house and tower at the mouth of the Ontonagon River on Lake Superior, lit 1852 or 1853, discontinued 1964 and now run by the county historical society.

structures.type: schoolhouse-style tower in a brick dwelling
structures.note: nine-foot-square tower in the lake-facing gable of a one-and-a-half-story brick dwelling (LighthouseFriends); the first building was a one-and-a-half-story stone dwelling with a short tower (LighthouseFriends)
eighteen-foot-square kitchen added to the rear of the dwelling (LighthouseFriends)

access.note: Visits by escorted tour from the Ontonagon County Historical Society museum (as LighthouseFriends lists it; not verified against the society's own site).

events.note: Station established 1852 (US Lighthouse Society Digital Archive place record). Rowlett's directory (via the station record) gives 1853; LighthouseFriends gives 26 August 1853 as the first keeper's appointment. Not resolved.
First keeper, Samuel Peck, appointed 26 August 1853 (LighthouseFriends)
Fifth-order Fresnel lens installed in the tower
Congress appropriated $14,000 on 7 April 1866; new brick dwelling with a tower in the gable; old lens moved to a new lantern room
Eighteen-foot-square kitchen attached to the rear of the dwelling
Town fire, 25 August 1896; the keeper's family kept the station's buildings wet and the light was saved (keeper's log as quoted by LighthouseFriends)
Patent conveying the lighthouse to the Ontonagon County Historical Society (act of Congress, 2000)
Over $100,000 spent in 2008 and 2009 on restoration

notes_for_editor: Thin primary record for the 1850s to 1880s: the Light-House Board volumes in the corpus begin in 1891, so the early history rests on LighthouseFriends (which quotes the keeper log and a 1916 newspaper) and the USLHS roster. First-light year unresolved: USLHS 1852, LighthouseFriends' first appointment 1853 (story gives both). The first building's material: LighthouseFriends says stone; Wikipedia (lead only, not cited) says wood; the 1866 brick tower date is LighthouseFriends' and differs from Wikipedia's 1867. The keeper-log and Ontonagon Herald quotations come through LighthouseFriends; the log and newspaper themselves were not read. Tour arrangements are as LighthouseFriends describes them (the page is undated); the society's own website did not resolve from this machine, so tour times were not checked. NRHP nomination 75000960 was not read (the NPGallery PDF returned no text; the NARA catalog is out of bounds). The Ontonagon Pierhead light is a separate station and is kept out of this story except for the 1899 storm entry. The Lighthouse Service Bulletin for 1936 says the two early radiobeacon installations, at Alpena and at Ontonagon, were still operating; it does not say which Ontonagon structure, so it is not used. Newspaper search for the 1896 fire returned nothing usable in an earlier pass; not repeated here. Keeper roster matched to the station by name and position (about 0.36 km); roster lines in this file match the archive's printed lines. Fact-check 2026-10-22: LighthouseFriends gives thirty-seven years for Corgan at this station against about thirty-six from the roster dates, now stated in the text; the 1901 and 1900 Board entries are read at scan pages 236 and 199 (printed pages not confirmed).
